title: Forensic Psychophysiologist (Polygraph Examiner) (GySgt to SSgt) NMOS (5821), DC I&L
raw_text:
9. MOS 5822, Forensic Psychophysiologist (Polygraph Examiner) (GySgt to
SSgt) NMOS (5821), DC I&L

    a. Summary. Psychophysiologists (Polygraph Examiners) perform the full
range of criminal investigative duties prescribed for and are operationally
assigned to the Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS).

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must currently hold MOS 5821.

            (2) Must be at least 25 years of age.

            (3) Must be a graduate of an accredited 4 year college.

        (4) Must have at least 2 years’ experience as a credentialed criminal
investigator (MOS 5821).

        (5) Prior to entry in the Polygraph Examiner Training Course, DoD
Polygraph Institute, must have sufficient obligated service to allow 36
months remaining upon graduation.

        (6) Must be screened and determined eligible for duty by an NCIS
Screening Board (as described in the most current version of the MOU between
the Director, NCIS, and CMC).

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Polygraph Examiner Training Course (A3558D3), DoD
Polygraph Institute, Ft Jackson, SC.

        (2) Certification will be accomplished by the Naval Criminal
Investigative Service (Code 23CP).

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and
Readiness Manual.




                                        3-336                          Enclosure (1)
 3136                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Detectives and Criminal Investigators 33-3021.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Criminal Investigator CID Agent, 5821.

CORRECTIONS 1. Introduction. The Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections OccFld provides the installation commander continuous support by enforcing the law, preventing and suppressing crime, assessing command physical security posture, preserving military control, quelling disturbances, investigating offenses, apprehending offenders, protecting property and personnel, investigating traffic accidents, controlling traffic, providing first response to active shooters incidents and special response to a barricaded subject, guarding military prisoners and supervising brig operations and correctional custody units. Provide the MARFORRES Commander support to security and mobility operations, battlefield circulation and traffic control, rear area security operations to include limited offensive and defensive combat operations, detention operations to include handling and safeguarding prisoners of war, refugees, or evacuees, guarding military prisoners, and returning absentees/deserters to military control.

9. MOS 5822, Forensic Psychophysiologist (Polygraph Examiner) (GySgt to SSgt) NMOS (5821), DC I&L a. Summary. Psychophysiologists (Polygraph Examiners) perform the full range of criminal investigative duties prescribed for and are operationally assigned to the Naval Criminal Investigative Service (NCIS). b. Prerequisites (1) Must currently hold MOS 5821. (2) Must be at least 25 years of age. (3) Must be a graduate of an accredited 4 year college. (4) Must have at least 2 years’ experience as a credentialed criminal investigator (MOS 5821). (5) Prior to entry in the Polygraph Examiner Training Course, DoD Polygraph Institute, must have sufficient obligated service to allow 36 months remaining upon graduation. (6) Must be screened and determined eligible for duty by an NCIS Screening Board (as described in the most current version of the MOU between the Director, NCIS, and CMC). c. Requirements (1) Complete the Polygraph Examiner Training Course (A3558D3), DoD Polygraph Institute, Ft Jackson, SC. (2) Certification will be accomplished by the Naval Criminal Investigative Service (Code 23CP). d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to reference (ac), Military Police, Investigations, and Corrections Training and Readiness Manual.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
